newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: British Aerospace may invest in UAE leasing firm.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace may invest in UAE leasing firm.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc's asset management arm is expected to take a 15 percent stake in a new leasing company with nominal capital of $136 million, based in the United Arab Emirates, industry executives said on Sunday.

UAE member Abu Dhabi on Sunday issued a decree setting up al-Waha International Leasing Co, which will seek leasing deals in the oil-rich Gulf region for a variety of high-ticket items such as commercial aircraft, ships, machinery and power plants.

British Aerospace "is expected to take a 15 percent stake as a strategic partner" in the company, providing wide expertise to the region's infant industry, one executive close to the new firm told Reuters.
The company will issue 50 million shares with a nominal value of 10 dirhams ($2.72) each.
Abu Dhabi state institutions, UAE founders and other Gulf institutions will have a 30 percent share. The founders are led by the UAE Offset Group and Abu Dhabi Investment Company (ADIC).
The remaining 55 percent of the company will be open to an initial public offering next month, said the executives, adding the board of directors would include two senior British Aerospace managers.
The emirate's Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) owns about 2.8 percent of British Aerospace, the sources said.
Abu Dhabi "feels that British Aerospace has a good and strong track record in asset management", one source said.
The founders had earlier this year shortlisted two global leasing firms as potential partners and also studied the possibility of hiring experts in the field to launch the new company on their own.

Abu Dhabi officials have said they expect the leasing concept to appeal to regional states which are trying to cut capital expenditure as their economies gradually recover from the high costs of the 1991 Gulf War and low oil prices.
